items.stem:
The diagram shows an isosceles trapezium.
The two sloping sides are equal in length.

parts.t: Write down the number of lines of symmetry of this trapezium.
Write down the order of rotational symmetry of this trapezium.

sols: A line of symmetry is a mirror line: folding along it makes the two halves match exactly.
Only the vertical line through the midpoints of the two parallel sides does this; a horizontal fold does not, because the parallel sides have different lengths.
Number of lines of symmetry = 1
Turn the trapezium about its centre through a full turn and count the positions in which it looks the same.
Only the starting position works, because a half turn swaps the long and short parallel sides.
Order of rotational symmetry = 1
every shape maps onto itself after a full turn

items.stem: This question is about the symmetry of quadrilaterals.

parts.t: Write down the number of lines of symmetry of a rhombus.
Write down the order of rotational symmetry of a parallelogram.
Write down the name of a quadrilateral that has exactly one line of symmetry and rotational symmetry of order 1.

sols: A rhombus has four equal sides, and its two diagonals are its mirror lines.
A fold along either diagonal makes the two halves match.
the sides of the rhombus are all equal
Number of lines of symmetry = 2
the sides themselves are not mirror lines
A parallelogram (not a rectangle or rhombus) has no line of symmetry, but it does have point symmetry about the point where the diagonals cross.
A half turn about that point maps each side onto the opposite side.
Order of rotational symmetry = 2
it looks the same after 180° and after 360°
A kite has one pair of equal opposite angles and one mirror line — the long diagonal.
Turning a kite through a half turn does not map it onto itself.
A kite
an isosceles trapezium is also acceptable
ms:
B1
oe, accept isosceles trapezium (trapezium with two equal sloping sides)

items.stem: The diagram shows a regular hexagon.

parts.t: Write down the number of lines of symmetry of a regular hexagon.
Write down the order of rotational symmetry of a regular hexagon.

A different regular polygon has 9 lines of symmetry.
Write down its order of rotational symmetry.

sols: A regular polygon with n sides has n lines of symmetry.
For the hexagon these are the 3 lines through opposite vertices and the 3 lines through the midpoints of opposite sides.
Number of lines of symmetry = 6
Each turn of 360 ÷ 6 = 60° maps the hexagon onto itself.
Order of rotational symmetry = 6
For any regular polygon the number of lines of symmetry and the order of rotational symmetry are both equal to the number of sides.
9 lines of symmetry means the polygon is a regular 9‑sided polygon.
Order of rotational symmetry = 9

items.stem: The diagram shows a shape drawn on a grid.

parts.t: Write down the number of lines of symmetry of the shape.
Write down the equation of each line of symmetry.
Write down the order of rotational symmetry of the shape.

sols: The shape folds onto itself about a vertical mirror and about a horizontal mirror.
A fold along either diagonal does not work, because the shape is not as tall as it is wide in the same way.
Number of lines of symmetry = 2
The shape stretches from x = 1 to x = 7, so the vertical mirror is halfway, at x = (1 + 7) ÷ 2 = 4.
It stretches from y = 0 to y = 6, so the horizontal mirror is at y = (0 + 6) ÷ 2 = 3.
The lines of symmetry are x = 4 and y = 3
The two mirror lines cross at (4, 3), and a half turn about that point maps the shape onto itself.
A quarter turn does not, because the shape is 6 wide and 6 high but the arms point up and down only.
Order of rotational symmetry = 2
ms:
B1 for x = 4
B1 for y = 3
B0 for ‘4’ or ‘3’ without x = / y =

items.stem: ABCDE is a regular pentagon with centre O.

parts.t: Write down the number of lines of symmetry of the pentagon.
Work out angle AOB.
Work out the size of one interior angle of the pentagon.

sols: Each line of symmetry passes through one vertex and the midpoint of the opposite side.
A regular polygon with n sides has n lines of symmetry.
Number of lines of symmetry = 5
The five angles at the centre are equal, because the pentagon has rotational symmetry of order 5.
Angle AOB = 360 ÷ 5 = 72°
Triangle OAB is isosceles with OA = OB.
both join the centre to a vertex
Angle OAB = (180 − 72) ÷ 2 = 54°
angle sum of a triangle
The interior angle at A is made of two of these equal angles, one from triangle OAB and one from triangle OAE.
by the line of symmetry through A
Interior angle = 2 × 54 = 108°
check: (5 − 2) × 180 ÷ 5 = 540 ÷ 5 = 108 ✓
ms:
M1 for 360 ÷ 5 = 72 then 180 − 72, or for (5 − 2) × 180 ÷ 5
A1 cao

items.stem: The curve y = x2 − 6x + 5 has one line of symmetry.

parts.t: Write down the equation of the line of symmetry of the curve.
Find the coordinates of the minimum point of the curve.

sols: Complete the square: x2 − 6x + 5 = (x − 3)2 − 9 + 5
half of −6 is −3
y = (x − 3)2 − 4
The squared bracket is unchanged when x is the same distance either side of 3.
Line of symmetry: x = 3
Check: the curve cuts the x‑axis where (x − 1)(x − 5) = 0, at x = 1 and x = 5, and 3 is halfway between them ✓
From y = (x − 3)2 − 4, the smallest value of (x − 3)2 is 0.
a square can never be negative
This happens when x = 3, giving y = −4.
on the line of symmetry
Minimum point = (3, −4)
ms:
M1 for (x − 3)2 − 4 oe, or for the roots 1 and 5 seen
A1 for x = 3, not just 3

items.stem: The diagram shows a cuboid measuring 5 cm by 5 cm by 8 cm.

parts.t: Write down the number of planes of symmetry of this cuboid.
Write down the order of rotational symmetry of this cuboid about the axis through the centres of the two square faces.
Write down the number of planes of symmetry of a square‑based pyramid.

A prism has a cross‑section that is an equilateral triangle.
Write down the number of planes of symmetry of this prism.

sols: Three planes cut the cuboid in half parallel to a pair of faces.
one for each pair of opposite faces
Because the cross‑section is a square, there are 2 more planes through the diagonals of the square faces.
these would not exist if all three lengths were different
Number of planes of symmetry = 3 + 2 = 5
The square face maps onto itself after each quarter turn.
Turning the cuboid through 90°, 180°, 270° and 360° about this axis gives the same solid each time.
Order of rotational symmetry = 4
Each plane of symmetry must contain the apex.
Two planes pass through the midpoints of opposite edges of the square base and two pass through opposite corners of the base.
Number of planes of symmetry = 4
the same as the number of lines of symmetry of the square base
The equilateral triangle cross‑section has 3 lines of symmetry, and each gives a vertical plane of symmetry of the prism.
There is also one horizontal plane halfway along the prism, parallel to the triangular ends.
Number of planes of symmetry = 3 + 1 = 4

A further 90°: (−1, 3) → (−3, −1)
this is the half turn of P
A further 90°: (−3, −1) → (1, −3)
The other two vertices are (−3, −1) and (1, −3)
Reflection in y = x swaps the coordinates: (x, y) → (y, x).

B1 for each correct point

A and B are points on a circle, centre O, radius 10 cm.
The chord AB has length 12 cm.
The line of symmetry of the circle through O and the midpoint M of AB meets the circle at C.

parts.t: Show that OM = 8 cm.
Calculate the area of triangle OAB.
Write down the length of MC.

sols: The circle is symmetrical about the line OMC, so this line bisects the chord AB at right angles.
the perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord
AM = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm and angle OMA = 90°.
In right‑angled triangle OMA: OM2 + 62 = 102
Pythagoras’ theorem, with OA = 10 cm a radius
OM2 = 100 − 36 = 64, so OM = √64 = 8 cm
Take AB as the base of triangle OAB; the perpendicular height is OM.
Area = <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub> × base × height = <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub> × 12 × 8
Area = 48 cm2
OC is a radius, so OC = 10 cm.
MC = OC − OM = 10 − 8 = 2 cm
M lies between O and C
ms:
M1 for AM = 6 with a right angle at M, and 102 − 62 oe
A1 for √64 = 8 nfww

items.stem:
A regular polygon has 15 lines of symmetry.
The polygon has centre O, and A and B are two vertices next to each other.

parts.t: Write down the order of rotational symmetry of this polygon.
Calculate the size of one interior angle of the polygon.
Calculate angle OAB.

A prism has this polygon as its cross‑section.
Write down the number of planes of symmetry of the prism.

sols: For a regular polygon, the number of lines of symmetry equals the number of sides, and equals the order of rotational symmetry.
15 lines of symmetry means 15 sides.
Order of rotational symmetry = 15
The exterior angles add up to 360°, so each exterior angle is 360 ÷ 15 = 24°.
Interior angle = 180 − 24 = 156°
interior and exterior angles are on a straight line
Check: (15 − 2) × 180 ÷ 15 = 2340 ÷ 15 = 156 ✓
Joining O to every vertex makes 15 congruent isosceles triangles, so angle AOB = 360 ÷ 15 = 24°.
by the rotational symmetry of order 15
Triangle OAB is isosceles with OA = OB.
Angle OAB = (180 − 24) ÷ 2 = 78°
angle sum of a triangle; it is also half of the interior angle, 156 ÷ 2 = 78 ✓
Each of the 15 lines of symmetry of the cross‑section gives a plane of symmetry at right angles to the ends.
There is one more plane, halfway along the prism and parallel to its ends.
Number of planes of symmetry = 15 + 1 = 16
ms:
M1 for 360 ÷ 15 = 24 seen, or for (15 − 2) × 180 ÷ 15
A1 cao

items.stem: Here are five capital letters drawn with straight strokes.

parts.t: Write down the letter that has exactly one line of symmetry.
Write down the letter that has exactly two lines of symmetry.
Write down all the letters that have rotational symmetry of order 2.

sols: Test each letter with a mirror line: M folds onto itself about the vertical line through its middle.
N, S and Z have no line of symmetry (a fold reverses the diagonal stroke); X has two.
Letter with exactly one line of symmetry: M
X has a vertical mirror line and a horizontal mirror line through its centre.
the diagonals are not mirror lines because the letter is taller than it is wide
Letter with exactly two lines of symmetry: X
Turn each letter through a half turn (180°) about its centre.
N, S, X and Z look exactly the same after a half turn; M does not (it becomes a W).
Letters with rotational symmetry of order 2: N, S, X, Z

items.stem: The diagram shows a pattern of shaded squares on a 4 by 4 grid.

parts.t: Write down the order of rotational symmetry of the shaded pattern.

Amir shades more squares so that the pattern has the vertical line through the centre of the grid as a line of symmetry.
Find the smallest number of extra squares he must shade.

sols: Turn the grid through 90°, 180° and 270°: the shaded squares never land on shaded squares.
Only the full turn returns the pattern to itself.
Order of rotational symmetry = 1
Every shaded square must have a mirror image on the other side of the vertical centre line.

The two shaded squares in the left half of the top row need images in the right half (2 squares); the shaded square in the second row needs one image; the square in the bottom‑left corner needs the bottom‑right corner.
none of the four shaded squares already has its image shaded
Smallest number of extra squares = 4
ms:
M1 for identifying the mirror image of at least two shaded squares
A1 cao

items.stem: Write down the answer to each part.

parts.t: The number of lines of symmetry of a semicircle.
The number of lines of symmetry of an equilateral triangle.
The name of a triangle that has no lines of symmetry.
The order of rotational symmetry of a circle.

sols: The only mirror line of a semicircle is the line through the centre of the diameter, perpendicular to the diameter.
the diameter itself is not a mirror line, because one side is curved and the other is straight
Number of lines of symmetry = 1
Each mirror line passes through a vertex and the midpoint of the opposite side.
Number of lines of symmetry = 3
a regular polygon with 3 sides
A triangle with three different side lengths cannot be folded onto itself.
A scalene triangle
A circle maps onto itself after a turn of any size about its centre.
Order of rotational symmetry = infinite

items.stem: This question is about the symmetry of shapes and regular polygons.

parts.t:
A shape has rotational symmetry of order 8.
Write down the smallest angle of rotation, greater than 0°, that maps the shape onto itself.

Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 30°.
Write down the number of lines of symmetry of this polygon.

A rotation of 72° about its centre maps a shape onto itself.
Write down the order of rotational symmetry of the shape.

sols: Order 8 means the shape looks the same 8 times in a full turn of 360°.
Smallest angle = 360 ÷ 8 = 45°
The exterior angles of a polygon add up to 360°, so it has 360 ÷ 30 = 12 sides.
A regular 12‑sided polygon has 12 lines of symmetry.
one for each side
Number of lines of symmetry = 12
The number of 72° turns in a full turn is 360 ÷ 72 = 5.
Order of rotational symmetry = 5

items.stem: The diagram shows a cube.

parts.t: Write down the number of planes of symmetry of a cube.
Write down the number of planes of symmetry of a cuboid whose length, width and height are all different.
Write down the number of planes of symmetry of a regular tetrahedron.

sols: Three planes cut the cube in half parallel to a pair of opposite faces.
Six more planes pass through a pair of opposite edges (each contains a diagonal of two opposite faces).
3 pairs of faces, each with 2 diagonals
Number of planes of symmetry = 3 + 6 = 9
Only the three planes parallel to the faces work; the diagonal planes do not, because no face is a square.
Number of planes of symmetry = 3
Each plane of symmetry contains one edge and the midpoint of the opposite edge.
A tetrahedron has 6 edges, so there are 6 such planes.
Number of planes of symmetry = 6

items.stem:
Triangle ABC is isosceles with AB = AC and angle BAC = 40°.
The dashed line from A is the line of symmetry of the triangle and meets BC at M.

parts.t: Write down the number of lines of symmetry of triangle ABC.
Work out angle ABC.
Write down angle AMB. Give a reason for your answer.

sols: An isosceles triangle has one mirror line, through the apex and the midpoint of the base.
Number of lines of symmetry = 1
The mirror line maps B onto C, so angle ABC = angle ACB.
base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal
Angle ABC + angle ACB = 180 − 40 = 140°
angle sum of a triangle
Angle ABC = 140 ÷ 2 = 70°
The line of symmetry is perpendicular to BC, because reflecting in AM maps B onto C.
Angle AMB = 90°
the line of symmetry is the perpendicular bisector of the base; check: 20 + 70 + 90 = 180 ✓
ms:
B1
90 and ‘line of symmetry is perpendicular to the base’ oe

items.stem:
ABCD is a rhombus. The diagonals AC and BD cross at O.
Angle ABC = 116°.

parts.t: Write down the number of lines of symmetry of the rhombus.
Work out angle ABO.
Work out angle BAO.

sols: The two diagonals of a rhombus are its lines of symmetry.
all four sides are equal
Number of lines of symmetry = 2
BD is a line of symmetry, so it bisects angle ABC.
reflecting in BD swaps A and C
Angle ABO = 116 ÷ 2 = 58°
The diagonals of a rhombus cross at right angles, so angle AOB = 90°.
AC is the mirror image of itself in BD, so AC ⊥ BD
In triangle ABO: angle BAO = 180 − 90 − 58
angle sum of a triangle
Angle BAO = 32°
check: angle BAD = 2 × 32 = 64 and 64 + 116 = 180, co‑interior angles ✓
ms:
M1 for angle AOB = 90 stated or used, or for (180 − 116) ÷ 2
A1 cao

items.stem: The pentagon in the diagram is made from a square of side 4 cm and an equilateral triangle of side 4 cm.

parts.t: Write down the number of lines of symmetry of the pentagon.
Work out the size of the interior angle of the pentagon at the point where the square meets the triangle.

A second equilateral triangle of side 4 cm is now joined to the opposite side of the square to make a hexagon.
Write down the number of lines of symmetry and the order of rotational symmetry of the hexagon.

sols: The vertical line through the apex of the triangle and the middle of the square is a mirror line; no other fold works because the triangle is only on one side.
Number of lines of symmetry = 1
At that vertex the angle of the square is 90° and the angle of the equilateral triangle is 60°.
Interior angle = 90 + 60 = 150°
With triangles on two opposite sides the shape has the vertical mirror line and also a horizontal mirror line through the middle of the square.
A half turn about the centre of the square also maps the shape onto itself, but a quarter turn does not.
the two remaining sides of the square are plain
2 lines of symmetry and rotational symmetry of order 2
ms:
B1 for 2 lines of symmetry
B1 for order 2

items.stem: This question is about the symmetry of solids.

parts.t: Write down the number of planes of symmetry of a prism whose cross‑section is a regular hexagon.
Write down the order of rotational symmetry of this prism about the axis through the centres of its two hexagonal ends.
Write down the number of planes of symmetry of a solid cylinder.

sols: Each of the 6 lines of symmetry of the hexagon gives a plane of symmetry running the length of the prism.
There is one more plane halfway along the prism, parallel to the two ends.
Number of planes of symmetry = 6 + 1 = 7
The regular hexagon has rotational symmetry of order 6, and every turn of 60° about the axis maps the prism onto itself.
Order of rotational symmetry = 6
Every plane containing the axis of the cylinder is a plane of symmetry, and there are infinitely many of these; there is also the plane halfway up, parallel to the ends.
Number of planes of symmetry = infinite

items.stem: The diagram shows a pattern of shaded squares on a 4 by 4 grid.

parts.t: Write down the order of rotational symmetry of the shaded pattern.
Write down the number of lines of symmetry of the shaded pattern.
Find the smallest number of extra squares that must be shaded so that the pattern has 4 lines of symmetry.

sols: Turn the grid through a quarter turn (90°) about its centre: each arm moves onto the next arm and the central block stays in place.
The pattern looks the same after 90°, 180°, 270° and 360°.
Order of rotational symmetry = 4
Every arm sticks out from its side of the central block in the same (anticlockwise) direction, so any mirror image has the arms going the other way round.
a ‘pinwheel’ has rotational but not line symmetry
Number of lines of symmetry = 0
For the vertical centre line to be a mirror, each arm needs its image: the four unshaded squares, one on each edge of the grid, must be shaded.
e.g. the top‑right arm reflects onto the top‑left square
With those four shaded the whole 4 by 4 grid is shaded, which has 4 lines of symmetry.
Smallest number of extra squares = 4
ms:
M1 for identifying the four unshaded edge squares, or a diagram with correct extra squares
A1 cao

items.stem:
ABCD is a kite with AB = AD and CB = CD.
Angle BAD = 70° and angle ABC = 100°.
The diagonals AC and BD cross at X.

parts.t: Write down the diagonal that is the line of symmetry of the kite.
Work out angle BCD.
Work out angle ABD.

sols: Reflecting in AC swaps B and D, because AB = AD and CB = CD.
The line of symmetry is the diagonal AC
BD is not a mirror line because AB ≠ CB
By symmetry angle ADC = angle ABC = 100°.
B and D are mirror images
The angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360°.
Angle BCD = 360 − 70 − 100 − 100 = 90°
Triangle ABD is isosceles with AB = AD, so angle ABD = angle ADB.
Angle ABD = (180 − 70) ÷ 2 = 55°
angle sum of a triangle; check: angle AXB = 180 − 35 − 55 = 90, the diagonals of a kite are perpendicular ✓
ms:
M1 for angle ADC = 100 stated or used
A1 cao

items.stem:
A shape has exactly two lines of symmetry, the lines x = 1 and y = −2.
One vertex of the shape is the point P(4, 3).

parts.t: Write down the coordinates of the image of P after reflection in the line x = 1.
Write down the coordinates of the other two vertices of the shape that correspond to P.
Write down the order of rotational symmetry of the shape and the coordinates of its centre of rotation.

sols: Reflection in x = 1 keeps y the same; 4 is 3 units to the right of 1, so the image is 3 units to the left of 1.
Image = (−2, 3)
Reflect P in y = −2: 3 is 5 above −2, so the image is 5 below, at y = −7.
Reflect that point in x = 1 as well: (4, −7) → (−2, −7)
The other two vertices are (4, −7) and (−2, −7)
Two perpendicular mirror lines give rotational symmetry of order 2 about the point where they cross.
reflecting in both lines is the same as a half turn
Order 2, centre (1, −2)

items.stem: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 150°.

parts.t: Show that the polygon has 12 lines of symmetry.

A prism has this polygon as its cross‑section.
Write down the number of planes of symmetry of the prism.

A pyramid has this polygon as its base and its apex directly above the centre of the base.
Write down the number of planes of symmetry of the pyramid, and the order of rotational symmetry of the pyramid about the vertical axis through its apex.

sols: Exterior angle = 180 − 150 = 30°
interior and exterior angles lie on a straight line
The exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360°, so the number of sides = 360 ÷ 30 = 12.
A regular polygon has as many lines of symmetry as sides, so it has 12 lines of symmetry.
6 through opposite vertices and 6 through the midpoints of opposite sides
Each of the 12 lines of symmetry of the cross‑section gives a plane of symmetry along the prism, plus one plane halfway along, parallel to the ends.
Number of planes of symmetry = 12 + 1 = 13
Every plane of symmetry must contain the apex and a line of symmetry of the base; there is no horizontal plane because the top and bottom are different.
Number of planes of symmetry = 12
A turn of 360 ÷ 12 = 30° about the vertical axis maps the pyramid onto itself.
Order of rotational symmetry = 12
ms:
M1 for 180 − 150 = 30 and 360 ÷ 30, or for (n − 2) × 180 ÷ n = 150 solved
A1 for 12 sides and the statement that lines of symmetry = number of sides

items.stem:
Two congruent squares have the same centre. One square is the image of the other after a rotation of 45° about the centre.
The outline of the two squares together forms a 16‑sided star.
A is a vertex of one square and B is a vertex of the other square.

parts.t: Write down the number of lines of symmetry of the star.
Write down the order of rotational symmetry of the star.
Write down the interior angle of the star at A.
Work out the reflex interior angle of the star at the point where a side of one square crosses a side of the other square.

sols: Each square has 4 lines of symmetry; the mirror lines of the two squares together give 8 different directions, 45° apart, and each is a mirror line of the whole star.
the star looks the same as a regular octagon with points
Number of lines of symmetry = 8
Turning through 45° maps the first square onto the second and the second onto the first, so the star maps onto itself.
360 ÷ 45 = 8, so the order of rotational symmetry = 8
A is a corner of a square, and the star has the same angle there as the square.
Interior angle at A = 90°
Where a side of one square meets a side of the other, the two sides are 45° apart, because one square is the other rotated through 45°.
The angle between the two sides on the outside of the star is 180 − 45 = 135°.
angles on a straight line
Reflex interior angle = 360 − 135 = 225°
check: the 16 angles are 8 × 90 + 8 × 225 = 2520 = (16 − 2) × 180 ✓
ms:
M1 for 135 seen, or 45 seen as the angle between the sides
A1 cao

items.stem:
ABCD is an isosceles trapezium with AB parallel to DC.
A is (−3, 0), B is (7, 0) and C is (5, 4).
The trapezium has one line of symmetry.

parts.t: Write down the equation of the line of symmetry.
Find the coordinates of D.
Calculate the area of the trapezium.
Calculate the length of BC. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
